note: CANVAS CONFORMANCE MANIFEST - the hand-authored denominator. Expected dispositions are written from the Figma documentation model's semantics (extract/figma/types.ts + the propose inversion rules' declared intent), NEVER from engine output. status:red = FAIL-EXPECTED-RED (doc model not met today; status quo pinned in observedCheck). A construct neither carried nor named-refused is a hard failure.

cases.construct: solid fill bound to a color variable on the variant root
cases.why: a var-bound solid paint is the canonical token binding (slash name inverts to a dot ref)

cases.construct: one node whose fill is a SOLID paint on some variants and an IMAGE on others
cases.why: absence of a solid is a capture GAP only where nothing on the node explains it. A node carrying an imageFill has a fully described paint stack - an image, and no solid under it that the capture saw - so its solid layer is an observation whose rendering-neutral literal is #00000000, exactly the reading the stroke channel already takes for a strokeless node. Both halves of the pair then carry over the whole axis. Before round 10 the mixed stack refused the WHOLE background-color channel, so Untitled UI's Avatar never rendered the #f9f5ff ground it draws on 108 of its 162 variants

cases.construct: raw (variable-less) solid hex fill on the root
cases.why: a raw paint is a hard drawn fact; mintUnbound mints a provisional imported.* token and binds it, never drops it

cases.construct: solid fill with paint alpha (dump v1.1 `alpha`)
cases.why: effective paint opacity is part of the drawn ink (Eventz 5%-black field case); must survive into the minted value

cases.construct: exactly one visible DROP_SHADOW in every variant
cases.why: the one effect form with a declared box-shadow projection (dump v1.2)

cases.construct: a TWO-layer drop-shadow stack on the root
cases.why: CSS box-shadow is natively a comma-separated LIST and the canvas emitter's stack grammar projects every layer back as its own native DROP_SHADOW, so a DROP_SHADOW-only stack has a lossless projection in both directions; refusing it (the pre-gap-round-4 rule) dropped the only visible edge of a light-on-light surface. BOTH layers must appear, in dump order — a truncation to one layer is still a failure

cases.construct: a two-value non-boolean variant axis with axis-correlated token bindings
cases.why: variant axes are enum props; per-variant refs differing in exactly the axis segment carry as ONE substituted ref

cases.construct: propRefs.characters binding a text node to a TEXT component property
cases.why: a characters propRef is the canvas spelling of a text prop; default comes from the bound node's characters

cases.construct: a text node riding the named TextStyle 'badge'
cases.why: a named TextStyle is a token identity; 'badge' inverts to the font.badge.size ref

cases.construct: a VECTOR child (arbitrary-path geometry) with a fill and a drawn fixed size
cases.why: arbitrary paths are outside dump v1 (parametric decor only); the capture receipts vector-geometry-unsupported and the node carries paints + box only

cases.construct: a non-NORMAL blendMode on the root (capture-boundary: no dump v1 field)
cases.why: blend modes have no dump projection; the capture receipts blend-mode-unsupported and nothing blend-shaped may appear in the contract

cases.construct: VERTICAL auto-layout with bound itemSpacing and symmetric bound padding
cases.why: mode VERTICAL inverts to direction column; bound itemSpacing to a gap ref; equal per-side pairs to padding-inline/-block

cases.construct: primary axis alignment SPACE_BETWEEN
cases.why: SPACE_BETWEEN is in the documented JUSTIFY inversion table

cases.construct: counter axis alignment BASELINE (a documented DumpLayout value)
cases.why: BASELINE is on the documented dump surface (DumpLayout.counter); text-and-icon rows drawn baseline-aligned should carry align: baseline (or at minimum a named refusal)
cases.observed: RE-RECORDED red -> green (canvas-fidelity gap-closing round 1, HEAD bd3843b). The SILENT LOSS is closed by CARRIAGE, not by a note. Mechanism: ALIGN_INV (core/propose-figma.ts:2548) held only MIN/CENTER/MAX, so the fourth documented DumpLayout.counter value fell through to undefined and invertLayout emitted direction only — no align, and nothing in the naming union. Fix: ALIGN_INV.BASELINE = 'baseline', and the align fact widened end-to-end on BOTH surfaces so the proposal is legal and renderable: LayoutSchema/VariantLayoutSchema align enum + ResolvedLayout (packages/schema/src/contract-schema.ts:114,140,1263) regenerated into contracts/contract.schema.json and packages/schema/contract.schema.json; ALIGN_CSS -> align-items: baseline (core/emit-react.ts:135, core/emit-html.ts:72, core/emit-react-inline.ts:72, packages/emitter-web-components/src/emit-wc.ts:170); ALIGN_FIGMA -> counterAxisAlignItems BASELINE (core/emit-figma-script.ts:922) with a VERTICAL guard in layoutSpec (:1070) because Figma throws on BASELINE under a column; roundtrip A_MAP (extract/figma/roundtrip.ts:77); COUNTER_CSS previews (extract/figma/canvas-gate/canvas-doc.ts:116, playground/src/engine/canvas-preview.ts:171). MEASURED: the two-text-child row now proposes anatomy.root.layout = {"display":"flex","direction":"row","align":"baseline"}. Every edit is a map key addition — zero committed dumps carry counter:BASELINE and zero committed contracts carry align:baseline, so no committed artifact moves.

cases.construct: literal (unbound) itemSpacing
cases.why: a drawn gap is a hard fact; mintUnbound mints a provisional gap token

cases.construct: left/right padding bound to DIFFERENT tokens
cases.why: an asymmetric pair carries as per-side longhand channels (padding-left/right) with a note, never refuses

cases.construct: a child drawn layoutSizingHorizontal FILL inside a ROW parent
cases.why: fillWidth in a row parent inverts to layout.grow on the part

cases.construct: every eligible child drawn FILL inside a COLUMN parent
cases.why: align: stretch is observable only through its artifact - every eligible child carrying FILL in a column parent

cases.construct: root primary axis drawn FIXED with an observed bbox (dump v1.5)
cases.why: a FIXED root dimension is otherwise unrecoverable (CBDS Dialog field case); the observed width mints as a root token

cases.construct: root drawn exactly at the generator default (row/center/center)
cases.why: the generator default is canvas-indistinguishable from no layout block; carriage-by-equivalence proposes NO layout (asserted by absence)

cases.construct: a width variable bound on the ROOT
cases.why: a component's outer dimension is fluid-up-to in code; a root-bound width inverts to max-width

cases.construct: literal minWidth/minHeight on the root (dump v1.4)
cases.why: a drawn minHeight 44 is a tap-target fact; carried as min-width/min-height style facts

cases.construct: uniform stroke bound to a color variable with a literal weight
cases.why: a var-bound stroke inverts to border-color; the literal uniform weight is a drawn fact and mints border-width

cases.construct: four equal stroke-weight bindings to one width variable
cases.why: four equal bound weights invert to one border-width ref

cases.construct: a stroke-only child (border, no fill at all)
cases.why: a stroke with no fill must carry as a border without inventing a background

cases.construct: per-side (non-uniform) stroke weights (capture-boundary: dump v1 carries a uniform weight only)
cases.why: the capture receipts stroke-weights-nonuniform; the proposal must not invent per-side widths

cases.construct: a stroke explicitly aligned INSIDE the node box (dump v1.11 captures the alignment of EVERY stroke)
cases.why: INSIDE is the alignment a CSS border already has - a border under box-sizing:border-box is drawn inward - so the stroke carries as border-color/border-width and nothing outline-shaped may appear. The case exists because before dump v1.11 this disposition rested on an ASSUMPTION about an absent field rather than a captured fact, and the same assumption was wrong elsewhere on the same canvas

cases.construct: a stroke aligned OUTSIDE the node box
cases.why: an OUTSIDE stroke grows the drawing beyond the node box without moving anything inside it; the only CSS spelling with that behaviour is an outline (drawn outside the border box, taking no layout space), so the pair carries as outline-color/outline-width and border-* must NOT appear - a border would draw the ring INWARD over the content, and growing the box to hold it instead moves the very node the drawing is anchored on

cases.construct: a stroke aligned CENTER (straddling the node box edge)
cases.why: a centred stroke draws half its weight inside the box and half outside; CSS border draws wholly inward and outline wholly outward, so neither spelling carries it exactly. The capture receipts stroke-align-unsupported under its OWN code - not folded into stroke-style-unsupported, which is what made this boundary uncountable for eight rounds - and the inversion NAMES the approximation instead of proposing an outline it cannot justify

cases.construct: a dashed stroke (dashPattern - capture-boundary)
cases.why: dashed strokes have no dump v1 projection; the receipt names it and the stroke renders solid

cases.construct: four equal radius bindings to one radius variable
cases.why: four equal bound radii invert to one border-radius ref

cases.construct: a literal uniform cornerRadius
cases.why: a drawn radius is a hard fact; mints a provisional border-radius token

cases.construct: per-corner (non-uniform) radii (capture-boundary: dump v1 carries a uniform radius only)
cases.why: the capture receipts radii-nonuniform; nothing corner-shaped may be invented

cases.construct: pixel-unit line height on a text node (dump v1.3)
cases.why: a px line height is captured verbatim (CBDS Tooltip field case) and mints line-height

cases.construct: style-less text whose (fontSize, fontStyle) matches MULTIPLE derived styles
cases.why: an ambiguous match must NOT adopt an identity - it is reported by count and the drawn values carry as minted literals

cases.construct: style-less text matching NO derived style
cases.why: a zero-match is reported and the drawn typography carries as minted literals, never guessed into a token identity

cases.construct: a NESTED part's channel that is a function of TWO variant axes (irreducible to either alone)
cases.why: A nested part's token that is a total function of TWO enum axes carries as a two-axis substituted ref. This fixture is deliberately WITNESSED — a third axis (Density) gives each Tone x Size cell two observations — so the correlation is corroborated and the carriage ships with NO caveat. Its saturated twin (token-nested-pair-saturated) holds the same construct at one observation per cell and must carry the SAME ref WITH a caveat; the pair of cases is what makes the caveat meaningful, since a caveat that appears on everything says nothing. Re-authored in gap-closing round 10.

cases.construct: the SAME two-axis nested channel at exactly one observation per cell (a SATURATED pair)
cases.why: A pair spanning |a| x |b| cells with no more than that many observations fits ANY values, so the correlation is unwitnessed — but every per-cell value is still MEASURED. Gap-closing round 10 first refused this case outright; measured against the kit, that discarded ButtonBase's twenty Size x Icon paddings and rendered a 22px-tall button where the canvas draws 40 — losing measured facts, the same class as border-color -> currentColor. The doctrine is therefore CARRY AND NAME: the ref reproduces the drawing exactly, and a caveat says the correlation is unwitnessed and may be drift rather than intent. This case pins BOTH halves — carriage and caveat — so neither a silent overclaim nor a silent loss can pass.

cases.construct: PERCENT/AUTO line-height unit (capture-boundary: only px is captured)
cases.why: non-px line-height units stay named receipts (text-channel-unsupported), never converted

cases.construct: node opacity (dump v1.2) on the root
cases.why: node opacity is distinct from paint alpha (Eventz disabled-variant field case) and mints an opacity binding

cases.construct: an ELLIPSE decor child (parametric shape, dump v1.3)
cases.why: ellipse is in the closed parametric-decor set; carries as a shape part with kind/width/height

cases.construct: a REGULAR_POLYGON decor child with a captured point count
cases.why: regular polygons are parametric; sides carries verbatim (CBDS Tooltip pointer field case)

cases.construct: a polygon whose point count was not captured (REST surface)
cases.why: the Figma default of 3 is assumed WITH a named review note, never silently

check.note: sides: 3 \(the Figma default, a triangle\) ASSUMED

cases.construct: a rotated RECTANGLE decor child (intrinsic size + CSS-clockwise rotation)
cases.why: rotated rects joined the parametric set in dump v1.3 (#42); rotation carries in CSS degrees

cases.construct: an ellipse with a constant partial arc sweep (dump v1.7 shape.arc)
cases.why: a constant partial sweep carries as shape.arc (conic-gradient mask on CSS surfaces; native arcData on the canvas)

check.note: constant ellipse arc sweep carried as shape\.arc

cases.construct: an ellipse arc with a FULL (2pi) sweep
cases.why: a full sweep is redundant with the plain ellipse - dropped BY NAME, the ellipse itself still carries

check.note: FULL sweep.*redundant with the plain ellipse, dropped

cases.construct: a partial arc with innerRadius > 0 (a donut/ring segment)
cases.why: the sweep and innerRadius carry as shape.arc; the filled-hole fraction and cap style are named residues

cases.construct: an ABSOLUTE plain rect with DumpShape x/y placement and constraints
cases.why: an out-of-flow rect carries position:absolute with minted offset channels picked from its constraints (LEFT/TOP -> left/top)

cases.construct: a FRAME child with dump v1.7 `abs` (layoutPositioning ABSOLUTE) in an auto-layout root
cases.why: the overlay-flattened class: position:absolute + offsets chosen from constraints (RIGHT/TOP -> right/top), root declared position:relative

cases.construct: a root WITHOUT auto-layout whose children all place by x/y (`abs`)
cases.why: a NONE-layout root owns positioned children: root carries its drawn box (bbox mints width/height) and each child carries absolute offsets; equal values dedupe into imported.shared.* leaves

cases.construct: an ABSOLUTE child whose constraints are SCALE x SCALE
cases.why: SCALE placement has no carried offset spelling (a stretch percentage, not an offset); must be a named refusal, the part renders in flow

check.note: constraint SCALE.SCALE has no carried offset spelling

cases.construct: an in-flow FIXED-size child that is not auto-layout, not abs, not decor (dump v1.8 fixedSize)
cases.why: the drawn box is a hard fact no other channel carries; width/height mint per axis

cases.construct: an image-paint FRAME captured BY HASH (dump v1.9 imageFill string) with a drawn fixed size
cases.why: the hash form names an exported asset; the documented carriage is background-image url + cover declarations on the part
cases.observed: RE-RECORDED red -> green (canvas-fidelity gap-closing round 1, HEAD bd3843b). The WRONG-NAME is closed at its source. Mechanism: isSpacer (core/propose-figma.ts:3222) tested fill/stroke/bound/text only, so a childless, paint-less image FRAME was classified a spacer; the spacer branch (:3941) carries layout and returns early, the part landed {}, its drawn 32px box was lost — while buildPart's note at :3603 still announced "IMAGE fill carried BY HASH". Fix: isSpacer now also refuses any node carrying imageFill or fixedSize (both absent-field no-ops, so a real spacer classifies exactly as before). MEASURED: the part carries tokens background-image = {imported.case.a.background-image} = url('./assets/images/3ba1c6f0aa.png'), width/height = {imported.case.a.width}/{imported.case.a.height} = 32px, and the declared cover triple (background-size: cover, background-position: 50% 50%, background-repeat: no-repeat); the note and the contract finally say the same thing. The CASE FILE was also corrected in the same pass: dump.plugin.js:429 writes figma's raw imageHash and imageFillCss appends the .png, so the old fixture's "3ba1c6f0aa.png" mis-modelled the capture surface and produced a .png.png URL; the case now holds the bare hash "3ba1c6f0aa". Byte-neutrality: a scan of all 3,982 FRAME nodes in every committed dump found exactly TWO childless paint-less frames carrying imageFill/fixedSize — this case and fill-image-bool.

cases.construct: an image-paint FRAME captured BY NAME only (imageFill: true)
cases.why: the documented carriage for the boolean marker is the neutral placeholder gradient rendered in the image's place
cases.observed: RE-RECORDED red -> green (canvas-fidelity gap-closing round 1, HEAD bd3843b). Same isSpacer trap as fill-image-hash, same one-line fix (core/propose-figma.ts:3222 now also refuses imageFill/fixedSize). MEASURED: the part carries background-image = {imported.case.a.background-image} = linear-gradient(135deg, #f2f4f7 0%, #d0d5dd 100%) — IMAGE_FILL_PLACEHOLDER_GRADIENT, the one documented spelling — plus the drawn 32px box as width/height mint observations. No cover triple here, by design: declareImageFillCover is hash-only (a placeholder gradient needs no background-size).

cases.construct: a gradient fill (capture-boundary: dump v1 carries solid paints only)
cases.why: the capture receipts paint-unsupported; no paint may be invented in the contract

cases.construct: a multi-paint fill stack (capture carries the first SOLID; the rest receipt paint-stack-truncated)
cases.why: truncation to the first solid is a declared limit with a receipt; the surviving solid still carries

cases.construct: a two-value variant axis whose options are literally true/false
cases.why: only a literal true/false axis is a boolean modeled the canvas way (isBoolAxis mirror)

check.note: true/false variant axis proposed as a boolean

cases.construct: a two-value Off/On axis (NOT literal true/false)
cases.why: Off/On stays a two-value enum (both states render truthfully) with a note that a code boolean is a compatible binding

check.note: a code boolean is a compatible code-side binding

cases.construct: a State=Default|Hover|Disabled axis (interaction-state vocabulary)
cases.why: interaction states are platform states, not API: hover promotes to a root state override, Disabled to a disabled boolean + state block, and the axis leaves the props

check.note: IS the platform's interaction states, not API

cases.construct: an interaction-state axis where one variant name omits the State pair
cases.why: promotion with incomplete pairs is unsafe - the near-miss must be a named refusal and the axis stays an enum prop

check.note: promotion unsafe, axis kept as an enum prop

cases.construct: a Theme=Light|Dark axis whose bound variables carry per-mode values (dump v1.6 modes)
cases.why: a corroborated mode axis is a token mode, not API (section 3): excluded from props, anatomy from the default mode only

check.note: IS a token-mode axis, not API

cases.construct: a Theme axis differing only in RAW color literals (no variables to ride)
cases.why: with no bound variables there are no modes for the deltas to ride - promotion is refused BY NAME and the axis stays an enum with per-value minted leaves

check.note: binds NO variables along the axis

cases.construct: a child present in exactly ONE value of an enum axis
cases.why: single-value presence reconstructs visibleWhen { prop, equals } (the Switch thumb-alignment discipline)

cases.construct: a child present in a strict SUBSET (2 of 3) of an axis's values
cases.why: subset presence carries as the value-subset visibleWhen form (equals: [..]), named in a note - never a silent omission

cases.construct: an empty, paint-less, binding-less fill-width frame between siblings
cases.why: the spacer idiom carries as a grow part (structural alignment, no ink)

cases.construct: a spacer present in only one value of an axis
cases.why: axis-correlated spacer presence reconstructs visibleWhen - how structural thumb alignment survives the round trip

cases.construct: the generator's auto-injected label artifact (root whose sole child is a children-bound text node)
cases.why: the label node is a generator artifact, not a part: its text tokens hoist to the ROOT and the bound prop proposes as `children`

cases.construct: the styled-static-text WRAPPER artifact (empty frame at the wrap default with fill + bound size)
cases.why: the wrap-default layout is elided; the frame proposes as a leaf part with tokens only (the Switch thumb)

cases.construct: three-deep nested frames each carrying their own facts
cases.why: nesting is ordinary anatomy: parts nest with their own layout/tokens at each level

cases.construct: a nested INSTANCE whose main component name matches an in-scope contract (no keys captured)
cases.why: a name match with no contradicting key evidence links the component ref, flagged verify-the-link

cases.construct: a RENAMED nested instance whose instanceSetKey matches a contract's componentSetKey anchor
cases.why: key identity survives renames (dump v1.5 session linking) - the key is checked FIRST, the drawn name is irrelevant

cases.construct: an instance named like an in-scope contract whose key CONTRADICTS that contract's anchor
cases.why: a foreign kit's Badge must not link to ds.badge on name coincidence - the link is refused BY NAME and an honest stub (suffixed id) takes its place

cases.construct: a nested instance with NO contract in scope, with observed bbox + primary paint
cases.why: the child ships as a STUB contract rendering the OBSERVED geometry via minted imported.stub-* tokens - a correctly-sized box, never invented anatomy

cases.construct: an unresolvable instance with NO observed geometry (pre-v1.5 dump shape)
cases.why: the ref + stub still propose; absent geometry stays a declared limit - no witness box may be invented

cases.construct: an applied component property tracking a parent enum axis 1:1 across variants
cases.why: a value that follows the parent axis threads as the placeholder "{parentProp}" instead of freezing one value

cases.construct: a constant applied component property on a linked instance
cases.why: fixed prop values ride componentProperties and canonicalize through the child contract's bindings (Success -> success)

cases.construct: a frame whose sole child is a Slot-utility instance bound to an INSTANCE_SWAP property
cases.why: the wrapper is a slot part; the utility's own styling is elided; first non-optional slot is judged the default (children)

check.note: Slot-utility instance styling is the utility's own

cases.construct: a slot wrapper with a 'Show <Property>' visibility binding
cases.why: the Show binding marks the part optional and is NOT an API prop

cases.construct: a NATIVE Figma slot node (Schema 2025, dump v1.5 type SLOT)
cases.why: native slots map to the same contract slot part with a provenance note so regeneration reproduces the native spelling

cases.construct: INSTANCE_SWAP preferredValues resolving to an in-scope contract by key
cases.why: preferred values resolve through anchors into accepts with acceptsMode prefer

cases.construct: preferredValues naming a key with NO in-scope contract
cases.why: unresolvable keys are named, never guessed into ids - accepts stays unauthored

cases.construct: a visibility-bound part visible in the default variant, with the set's BOOLEAN defaultValue captured (dump v1.5 boolDefaults)
cases.why: the boolean prop default comes from the captured property definition - the one default variants alone cannot recover

cases.construct: a visibility-bound part HIDDEN in the default variant (dump v1.1 hidden, producer stamps dumpVersion)
cases.why: hidden-in-default is positive evidence for default false (never inverted into true without the producer marker)

cases.construct: rotation on a non-decor node (capture-boundary: rotation rides shape decor only)
cases.why: the capture receipts rotation-unsupported; the node renders unrotated and nothing rotation-shaped may be invented

cases.construct: an observed subtree paint on an instance LINKED to a real contract (classic path, no instanceOverrides ledger)
cases.why: the child contract owns its paint; a per-usage override is not representable on a component ref without the opt-in override machinery - ledgered by name

check.note: per-usage paint override is not representable

cases.why: inner shadows are outside the DROP_SHADOW-stack grammar (a stack of DROP_SHADOW layers carries comma-separated; INNER_SHADOW does not) - the channel is NAMED by kind, not proposed

cases.construct: a LAYER_BLUR effect on the root
cases.why: blur types carry type/radius only so the gap can be NAMED - no filter/box-shadow may be proposed

cases.construct: a drop shadow on a TEXT node
cases.why: a text shadow has no contract vocabulary (box-shadow is a box channel) - named, not proposed
